messages.subject: HIERARCHICAL GAUSSIAN  SPATIO TEMPORAL MODELS
parts:
Hell Stan Team,

Thanks for your previous direction, I got a lot of help with defining my covariance. The forum guys are taking a bit long.

Generally, we are trying to  model an underlying Gaussian Process with binomial sampling distribution(likelihood). Our models

are hierarchical over the parameters, Bk,which I give a joint normal prior and over hyper-parameters of the covariance matrix. We approximate the spatial dependency using the non-stationary,

anisotropic matern covariance ,whose parameters : length-scale(rho) and signal-variance(sigma-squared) are given the inverse_gamma(0.001,0.001) and uniform(0,200) priors

respectively.

Specifically my target model is: "glmm-model.png"- attached in this post.



#Now if fj is an Auto-regressive dynamics- for example, when each observation was made at a yearly time-point, which is very important for our inference- then I prefer to model it using an ar model or a random-walk ,where most appropriate.

 

#My Challenge

I have set up the model as given in the attached script, apparently it gives back results that are not consistent with the expected/known trend. I thought first to diagnose convergence but ended up with inconsistent volatility across the sampling chains. I suspected my initial parameterization values to be a possible cause and have since given different permutations of priors and inits, including specifying flat priors but the convergence is not clearly coming out.

 

I would like you to help me preview my model specification if it is indeed consistent with the literature of gaussian hierarchical models especially as specified in this mail, or even point to an unintentional failure that might have occurred. Your comments are highly regarded! I have attached an example dataset(Sl_ageCorrected*), stan model(sl_multigp.stan)  with prediction raster files: (sl_prec.asc,sl_urb.asc). You can also see the surface prediction I got initially(sl_PR_180615)

 

Kind Regards!

Lukio

That particular syntax error is because in transformed data you need to declare everything before doing any assignments. For example, you have 

 ...
 int<lower=2> N;
N<- N_obs + N_new;

vector[D] x[N];
 ...

but you can't assign a value to N until after declaring x, etc.

parts:
Also, that's true in the other blocks that allow assignment too. The exception is that you can make new declarations in local blocks. For example:

model {
 real a;
 real c;
 a <- 2;
 {
  real b;
  b <- 2;
  c <- a + b;
 }
}

is ok, but 

model {
 real a;
 real c;
 a <- 2;
 real b;
 b <- 2;
 c <- a + b;
}

will give you an error.
